# Teme developer handbook

Guides for people and agents who build Teme plugins and themes. Reference under docs/reference/ is generated; these pages are written and tested against the code.

- [Plugin or theme?](start/plugin-or-theme.md): Which package you need — a plugin that adds behavior, or a theme that draws the public site.
- [Your first plugin](start/first-plugin.md): From an empty folder to an enabled plugin that listens to a hook.
- [Your first theme](start/first-theme.md): A theme with an index template and a single template, from the handbook example.
- [Set up a development site](start/development-site.md): One local Teme site that loads every plugin and theme you are building, straight from their own folders.
- [The manifest](concepts/manifest.md): How to write teme-plugin.json and teme-theme.json, and where the key tables live.
- [Hooks](concepts/hooks.md): The five verbs, the after-commit rule, capabilities, what happens when a listener fails, the Since version and requires.teme, and where the generated hook list lives.
- [Operations](concepts/operations.md): Every change goes through an Operation; what a plugin may and may not touch.
- [Code standards for plugins and themes](start/code-standards.md): What Teme requires of a plugin's or theme's code, what it only recommends, and where Teme's own coding standards are.
- [Testing a plugin or theme](testing.md): How to test a plugin or theme with Pest and Teme's testing kit, against a real Teme site, through the same checks the admin makes.
- [Plugin settings and secrets](plugins/settings.md): How a plugin declares its settings screen in the manifest, splits it into sections, shows a setting only when another has a value, keeps lists and markup, reads and writes its values, keeps API keys as secrets, reaches hosts a person types into them, adds actions and lists to the page, and adds a Tools link.
- [Your plugin's own tables](plugins/tables.md): How a plugin creates tables of its own with migrations, the names they must have, how they are read and written, run after an update, and removed.
- [Regions, site code and featured posts](themes/regions.md): How a theme sets aside regions for the site's own content, where an administrator's own HTML goes, and how to draw pinned posts on the latest posts page.
- [Rules for plugins and themes](rules/plugins-and-themes.md): The rules every plugin and theme lives by, both the ones Teme enforces and the ones authors must keep because Teme cannot check them.
- [Listing your plugin or theme in Teme's directory](start/publishing.md): How a plugin or theme gets into Teme's free directory, so every Teme site can find and install it from Add plugin or Add theme.
- [For agents](for-agents.md): How agents should read this handbook and llms.txt, choose a plugin's capabilities, and write an AGENTS.md for it.
- [Plugins writing content](plugins/content-write.md): How a plugin granted content.write creates, changes, publishes, unpublishes and schedules items, with their slugs, credits and language versions, always on behalf of a named person.
- [Reading content](plugins/content-read.md): How a plugin with content.read lists the site's published items a page at a time, and reads an item's draft and the queue of unpublished items for the person its work acts for.
- [What visitors send from a public form](plugins/submissions.md): How a plugin with content.submissions keeps what a visitor sends from its public form as an item waiting for review, written as the site itself, and how Teme limits how many it takes.
- [Reading Teme's directory](plugins/directory.md): How a plugin with directory.read reads the plugins and themes Teme's directory lists, as Teme verified them, and why an answer may be empty.
- [Adding redirects from a plugin](plugins/redirects.md): How a plugin with the redirects capability adds, lists and removes its own redirects, which Teme writes as the site and marks on Tools › Redirects, and what it can never touch.
- [Creating terms from a plugin](plugins/terms.md): How a plugin with the terms.write capability creates, updates, lists and removes terms of the taxonomies it brought, and what it can never touch.
- [Sending files and raw bodies](plugins/outbound-files.md): How a plugin with http sends a multipart upload with files, or a raw body whose exact bytes it signs, through the outbound door, and the 10 MB limit on what it sends.
- [Jobs and schedules](plugins/jobs.md): How a plugin declares background jobs and schedules in its manifest, queues them, after a delay or once while one waits, writes their handlers, when a schedule is due, who a run acts for, schedules its own settings switch and time, every limit a run works within, and what happens when one fails.
- [Console commands from a plugin](plugins/commands.md): How a plugin declares console commands in its manifest and answers them through HasCommands, so a job it schedules can also be run by hand, and what Teme guarantees about when they exist and who runs them.
- [Public routes](plugins/public-routes.md): How a plugin answers addresses on the public site, which paths it may take, how inbound posts are verified, cached and limited, what Teme answers before a handler runs, and which addresses Teme answers itself.
- [Files at the site's root](plugins/root-files.md): How a plugin declares a small text file at the site's root, such as a verification key, which core serves without running the plugin's code.
- [Scripts for a plugin's output](plugins/scripts.md): How a plugin ships a built script for its cards and its page insertions, so Teme serves it and links it only on a public page that shows that output, and only when the site allows the plugin to run code in visitors' browsers.
- [The plugin import socket](plugins/import.md): How a plugin brings its own data across when a site moves from WordPress, declaring exactly what it reads and receiving it from Teme's import.
- [Import readers](plugins/import-readers.md): How a plugin teaches Teme's import engine to read another system's export file, so that the engine's plan, runs, map, report and redirects serve that system as they serve WordPress.
- [Content inside articles](plugins/insertions.md): How a plugin with content.insert places markup between an article's blocks, such as ads, and what core cleans, caps and leaves out.
- [Content on every page](plugins/page-insertions.md): How a plugin with pages.insert places markup in the head, at the top and bottom of every page, between list items, around a theme's regions and fixed to the screen's edge, and what core cleans, caps and leaves out.
- [Cards for a theme's regions](plugins/cards.md): How a plugin with pages.insert offers cards that editors place in a theme's regions, with fields core draws, options it gives while a card is filled in, and markup it draws on the public page.
- [Stylesheets for a plugin's output](plugins/styles.md): How a plugin ships a built stylesheet for its cards and its page insertions, so Teme serves it, wrapped in its own cascade layer, only on a page that shows that output.
- [The fediverse](plugins/fediverse.md): What core does on the fediverse by itself, and the sockets a plugin can use to hear activities, handle them, change what is sent, and send its own.
- [List columns](plugins/list-columns.md): How a plugin adds a column to the admin's content lists.
- [List actions](plugins/list-actions.md): How a plugin adds row and bulk actions to the admin's content lists.
- [Feeds and the site](plugins/feeds-and-site.md): How a plugin adds links to the site's feeds, reads the site's address, name, language and feeds, hears which feeds a change touched, and posts a form to a service outside the site.
- [The site's AI connection](plugins/ai.md): How a plugin asks the site's own AI connection for the tasks it declares, and what Teme records and limits for it.
- [Your own hooks, and plugins that need other plugins](plugins/your-own-hooks.md): How a plugin declares hooks of its own for other plugins, sends them through HookSender, and how an add-on requires the plugin it extends and listens to those hooks.
- [Check an item before it is saved](plugins/before-save.md): How a plugin is asked before an item is saved or published, how it refuses a save with a reason, and what happens when its check fails or runs too long.
- [Notices from plugins](plugins/notices.md): How a plugin with notices.send declares kinds of notice, who each reaches, and what Teme lets a notice say and how many it sends.
- [A plugin's own area](plugins/admin-area.md): How a plugin declares screens of its own in the admin, an overview of figures and charts, tables of its records and each record's form, what core draws and checks, the permission that opens them, and the PluginArea contract that hands core the data.
- [Panels on Home](plugins/home-panels.md): How a plugin adds panels to the admin's Home screen, built from blocks of its own area, who sees them, what happens when a block can't be read, and how a person hides or moves a panel.
- [A panel in the editor](plugins/editor-panels.md): How a plugin that works on the article being edited adds a panel to the editor, what the panel shows, how its actions start the plugin's work as the person, and how each suggestion is checked, used and undone.
- [Search engine plugins](plugins/seo.md): How an SEO plugin adds checks beside the editor's own, a tab of its own values in Search and social, tags and structured data in the head of public pages, and sitemaps to the sitemap index, and how it reads the FAQ and Steps cards to describe them.
- [An image service](plugins/image-service.md): How a plugin gives the address of each image size from an outside image service, one that resizes or converts images when they are asked for, in place of the sizes core made at upload.
- [Provider slots](plugins/provider-slots.md): How a plugin fills a provider slot, a service that needs exactly one active provider, and how the administrator picks which one.
- [A comment check](plugins/comment-check.md): How a plugin judges each comment before it is saved, as a spam check does, with core's moderator still applying its own lists after the plugin's verdict.
- [A search engine](plugins/search-engine.md): How a plugin answers the site's searches from its own engine, such as an outside index, with core's search standing in whenever the engine fails or is slow.
- [Your plugin's data in the site export](plugins/exports.md): How a plugin adds a file of its own to the site's export, so what it keeps leaves with the site's content, and what happens when it fails.
- [Content types from your plugin](plugins/content-types.md): How a plugin brings its own content types, taxonomies and fields in a teme-types file, what happens on enable, update, disable and removal, and how it takes over types a site already has.
- [Languages in a theme](themes/languages.md): What a multilingual site gives a theme, from the page's language and direction, its other language versions, the language switcher, and the theme's own words.
- [Addresses, listings and bodies in a template](themes/template-data.md): The values and tags a template can read for the site's own addresses, breadcrumbs, a page's siblings, a type's items, a listing's totals, reading time, search sections, heading ids and a contents list, the body's blocks, and for knowing which region a card is drawn in.
- [Scripts in a theme under the page policy](themes/scripts.md): What a theme's JavaScript may do under Teme's content security policy, the compressed script budget, and how the default theme stays small.
- [Archive pages, author profiles and listing data](themes/archive-pages.md): What a theme reads on a type's archive page and an author's page, and how its script asks for search suggestions and for any listing's next page as data.
- [Tokens, styles and fonts](themes/tokens-and-styles.md): How a theme declares core tokens, its own custom tokens, named style variations, fonts with face and unicode_range, and how the site brand colour becomes --teme-brand.
- [Overriding core's components](themes/components.md): How a theme replaces one of the six pieces core draws on every page, which data each one hands its view, what a comment-form override must keep, and how the contract number keeps an override in step with core.
- [The management API](outside/management-api.md): For a service outside the site, not a plugin, with keys and abilities, the endpoints, the problems it answers, and its limits.
